Focus on Indonesia's accelerated infrastructure spending under the new administration and rising private investment in toll roads and ports as durable catalysts.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Rising middle-class healthcare spending in Indonesia, with private insurance penetration growing at 8% CAGR, underpins sustained demand for hospital and diagnostic services.
Government push for domestic pharmaceutical self-sufficiency, via mandatory local sourcing and tax incentives, creates long-term tailwinds for Indonesian drug manufacturers like SRAJ.
Medical tourism expansion, targeting 5 million foreign patients by 2025, boosts premium hospital chains and specialized care providers in Jakarta and Bali.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's healthcare sector shows relative strength (+0.72%) versus US weakness, signaling domestic resilience. Key movers like SRAJ and MICE indicate local demand momentum. Capitalize on this divergence by overweighting Indonesian hospital and pharma names, as structural underpenetration and rising medical tourism drive durable growth.

sectors.name: Logistics

Domestic consumption resilience, supported by a young population and rising middle class, provides a durable demand base for logistics services, insulating the sector from global trade slowdowns.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's logistics sector shows strong local momentum (+1.92%) versus US weakness, signaling potential decoupling. Focus on domestic demand-driven names like KJEN and BULL, which surged on e-commerce and infrastructure tailwinds. Watch for sustained volume confirmation before adding exposure, as US headwinds may still spill over.

Rising formalization of the informal economy is accelerating digital ad spend, benefiting VIVA and FUTR as key beneficiaries of programmatic and mobile-first advertising.
sectors.ai: Aggressively rotate into Indonesia's entertainment and media names, as MDIA's +34.62% surge and broad sector strength (+2.93% ID vs -1.65% US) signal a structural re-rating on domestic consumption and digital ad growth. Capitalize on the divergence from US weakness by overweighting Jakarta-listed names with exposure to infrastructure-linked projects and affordable housing mandates.
